answer: Proof of Personhood protocols mandate that an agent verify its unique biological or verifiable digital signature at the dawn of its entry into the network. By sequestering identity tokens within a cryptographic vault, the system forces an attacker to incur the heavy cost of acquiring authentic biometric attestations for each node. This threshold requirement flattens the mesa of low-cost malicious replicas, ensuring that Sybil attacks remain economically irrational due to the scarcity of human-verified credentials.
